title: Madhuri Dixit Just Conquered Netflix. Maa Behen Is the #2 Film on the Planet and It's Not Slowing Down.
excerpt: A dead body, three dysfunctional women, and the most subversive Hindi film of 2026 — now trending in 15 countries with Priyanka Chopra and Vidya Balan singing its praises.
body:
The numbers are in, and they're staggering. Eight days after its quiet debut on Netflix, **Maa Behen** — a film built on nothing but three extraordinary women and a dead body — has climbed to the #2 spot on Netflix's Global Top 10 Non-English Films list. It's trending in 15 countries. The internet is quoting its punchlines back to itself. And somewhere in the middle of all this chaos, **Madhuri Dixit** is doing the best work she's done in years.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=xYbLpsEhcfA</youtube>

Let's start with what makes this film so deliciously dangerous. Directed by **Suresh Triveni** — the man behind *Tumhari Sulu* and *Jalsa* — *Maa Behen* follows Rekha (Madhuri), a widow living in a dingy apartment where the neighbours have already decided she's a witch. Her crime? Wearing sleeveless clothes. Smiling too confidently. Refusing to shrink. When her neighbour Gupta Ji (played with sleazy perfection by **Ravi Kishan**) turns up dead in her house one night, Rekha makes a panicked midnight call to her two daughters, and the real film begins.

> "From the very beginning, Maa Behen was about exploring unusual family dynamics, flawed yet deeply relatable characters, and the societal judgments that shape their lives — all through humour and chaos." — Suresh Triveni

**Triptii Dimri** plays Jaya, the married daughter whose powerful monologue about identity has already become one of the most talked-about scenes of 2026. **Dharna Durga** — a relative newcomer — plays Sushma, a Patna-based content creator whose #JijuMeinJauu catchphrase is currently taking over Instagram reels. Together, the three of them navigate a body, a cover-up, and the suffocating judgment of a society that scrutinises every breath a woman takes.

The genius of *Maa Behen* is in its tonal tightrope. It's a crime comedy that never lets you forget it's a satire. The characters are named after the *Washing Powder Nirma* jingle — Rekha, Jaya, Sushma — "sabki pasand," all marketed to women, all consumed by the household. The title itself is a wink: "Maa Behen," the most common expletive in Hindi, weaponised right back at the patriarchy that invented it.

Madhuri is magnetic here. She plays Rekha with a looseness we've never quite seen from her — a woman who has buried her husband and her reputation but refuses to bury her desires. Her viral delivery of "Mujhe Garmi Lagti Hai" (a line that sounds innocent until you realise it's anything but) has already spawned a thousand memes. This isn't the Madhuri of *Devdas* or *Dil To Pagal Hai* — this is an actress who's stopped trying to be lovable and started being honest. She's never been better.

The Bollywood establishment has noticed. **Priyanka Chopra Jonas** posted an Instagram story calling the film "sharp, funny and so well done" and singled out Dharna Durga: "I have been such a fan always, and I cannot wait to see what all you unleash upon us." **Vidya Balan** — who starred in Triveni's *Tumhari Sulu* — added her own endorsement, praising the "crackling chemistry" between the three leads.

**For the diaspora, this is the easiest recommendation of the month.** *Maa Behen* is streaming now on Netflix worldwide — no geo-restrictions, no VPN gymnastics. It's 127 minutes, it's in Hindi, and it's the kind of film that'll make you laugh until it makes you furious. The only film ahead of it on the global chart is the Spanish thriller *The Marked Woman*, and at this rate, even that lead feels temporary.

Triveni has built something genuinely rare: a commercial entertainer that has teeth. The pulpy editing (courtesy Dipika Kalra), the slow-motion sequences that force you to stare at what you'd rather look away from, the VFX that turns a cramped apartment into a pressure cooker — it all works because the performances ground it. Madhuri carries the secrets, Triptii carries the fury, and Dharna carries the laughs. Together, they've made the most talked-about Indian film on the planet right now.

And if you haven't watched it yet, what exactly are you waiting for?
